Raw block references of a multidimensional array

Source: R/gdal_mdim.R
mdim_block_refs.Rd

mdim_block_refs() returns the location of the stored blocks (chunks) of an array of a GDAL Multidimensional Raster dataset: for each block, the file that contains it, and the byte offset and size of the block in that file. The blocks are not read or decoded. This is the information needed to fetch the raw bytes of a block directly (e.g., with a byte range request), or to build a table of references to the blocks of a set of files (a "virtual" dataset in the style of kerchunk or VirtualiZarr). Requires GDAL >= 3.12. This function is experimental. Its interface may change in future releases.

Usage

mdim_block_refs(x, start = NULL, count = NULL)

Arguments

x

An object of class GDALMDArray.

start

Optional numeric vector of 0-based start indexes of a hyperslab, one value per dimension.

count

Optional numeric vector giving the number of values of a hyperslab along each dimension. Required if start is given.

Value

A data frame with one row per block. For an array of n dimensions, the first 3 * n columns are those of mdim_chunk_index() (chunkoff0, ..., off0, ..., size0, ...), followed by:

  • filename: the file that contains the block, or NA

  • offset: the offset in bytes of the block in that file, or NA

  • size: the size in bytes of the block as stored, or NA

  • info: list column of character vectors of driver-specific NAME=VALUE pairs that describe how the block is encoded

  • inline_data: list column with a raw vector for a block that the dataset holds inline (filename and offset are then NA), otherwise NULL

A block that is missing in the dataset (all values are nodata) has NA for filename, offset and size.

Details

The blocks are those of mdim_chunk_index() with the block size of the array as stored, optionally limited to the blocks that intersect a hyperslab given by start and count. Their locations are obtained with $getRawBlockRefs() of class GDALMDArray (see that method for details of the values returned and the formats supported).

The time needed depends on the format. For netCDF-4 and HDF5, the index of blocks in the file is read once. For Zarr, each block is a file (or a part of a file) that GDAL has to query, so a remote store takes one or more network requests per block. Use start and count to limit the number of blocks.

See also

GDALMDArray, mdim_chunk_index(), mdim_read()

Examples

f <- system.file("extdata/mdim_small.nc", package="gdalraster")
ds <- new(GDALMultiDimRaster, f)
arr <- ds$openMDArray("/t2m")

# this array is stored as one block, not compressed
refs <- mdim_block_refs(arr)
refs[, c("filename", "offset", "size")]
#>                                                           filename offset size
#> 1 /home/runner/work/_temp/Library/gdalraster/extdata/mdim_small.nc   2040  240
refs$info[[1]]
#> [1] "ENDIANNESS=LITTLE"

# the bytes of the block, read directly from the file and decoded
con <- file(refs$filename[1], "rb")
invisible(seek(con, refs$offset[1]))
b <- readBin(con, "raw", n = refs$size[1])
close(con)
v <- readBin(b, "integer", n = length(b) / 2, size = 2, endian = "little")
v[v == arr$getNoDataValue()] <- NA

identical(v, arr$read(NULL, NULL, NULL))
#> [1] TRUE

arr$close()
ds$close()
